subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: Should gateway startup keep failing closed on required SecretRef resolution failures, add a bounded in-process retry/backoff policy, or introduce a degraded-startup/circuit-breaker mode for external exec secret providers?
rationale: The source-level problem is clear, but the fix changes security and availability semantics for required credentials and could either reduce crash-loop amplification or mask credential failures too long.

options.title: Bounded generic startup retry
options.body: Add a small default retry/backoff around startup SecretRef preparation, keep final failure fail-closed, and document that provider-specific caching belongs in resolvers/plugins.

options.title: Explicit degraded-startup policy
options.body: Allow startup to remain online with unavailable SecretRefs only after a maintainer-approved policy defines which surfaces may degrade and how operators are alerted.

options.title: External resolver/plugin only
options.body: Leave core fail-fast behavior unchanged and document resolver-level caching/batching such as Varlock for quota-sensitive providers.

recommendation.title: Bounded generic startup retry
recommendation.body: Add a small default retry/backoff around startup SecretRef preparation, keep final failure fail-closed, and document that provider-specific caching belongs in resolvers/plugins.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail for eager SecretRef activation and reload degradation behavior points to this contributor.
